samples.summary: New tab-delete route bypasses the key-membership guard this change centralises: `resolveDelete` still uses a truthiness test on `root.tabs?.[tabId]`
samples.evidence:
The diff's whole premise (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-lookup.util.ts:36-45`, and `tabs.controller.ts:259` which does use `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(root.tabs)`) is that a truthiness test on a record entry is not an existence test: on a live Yorkie `JSONObject` proxy the get trap answers `toJSON` / `toJS` / `toJSForTest` / `toString` / `getID` with a truthy *function*.

The newly added `DELETE .../tabs/:tabId` does NOT go through that guard. `packages/backend/src/api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:172` calls `resolveDelete`, and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:78` is `const tab = root.tabs?.[tabId]; if (!tab) return {ok:false,reason:'not_found'}`. For `tabId = 'toJSON'` on a live document that is truthy, so the handler proceeds: `resolution.name` is `undefined` and `applyDelete` (`tab-ops.ts:103-104`) runs `delete root.tabs['toJSON']` and, if `root.sheets?.['toJSON']` is likewise truthy, `delete root.sheets['toJSON']` inside `doc.update` — Yorkie routes `delete` to `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which throws `fail to find <key>` for a key that was never set (the diff itself documents this trap in `comment-ops.ts#applySetResolved`). Result is a 500 with an aborted CRDT transaction instead of a 404, on the exact input class this change exists to close.

The new `tabs.controller.spec.ts` cannot catch it: its fixture root is a plain object, where `tabs['toJSON']` is `undefined`.

The same pattern is left in `resolveRename` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:216`, `const tab = tabs?.[tabId]`) reached from `tabs.controller.ts:131`, so `PATCH .../tabs/toJSON` is out of step too (pre-existing, but not updated while every `sheets` lookup was). Fix belongs in `resolveDelete`/`resolveRename` (or their call sites) using `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(root.tabs).includes(tabId)`, matching `tabs.controller.ts:259`.

samples.summary: Second board-root type and a docblock that now states the opposite of what the code does
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/template/seed/board.ts:13` declares `BoardRoot { meta: { title: string }; elements: SlidesElement[] }`, and its docblock at lines 6-9 asserts "There is no backend writer for boards the way there is for docs / slides / notes — `PUT /documents/:id/content` covers only those three — so the seed assigns this shape directly." This diff adds exactly that writer (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/board-tree.ts` + `docs-content.controller.ts:222-232`), so the comment is now false and there are two mirrors of `YorkieBoardRoot` in the backend (`BoardRoot` and `BoardYorkieRoot`) that will drift — `BoardRoot.meta` already lacks the `unit` / `recentColors` fields `BoardMeta` carries. `seed-templates.ts:109-118` still assigns `root.meta`/`root.elements` by hand rather than calling `writeBoardRoot`.

samples.summary: Top-level design docs still state that comments have no `/api/v1` controller and that the client is the only comment writer
samples.evidence: `docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md:213` records "Comments | 6 | No comment controller under `/api/v1`; comments live in the Yorkie CRDT and never pass through the backend" — the capability-audit row this change is explicitly closing (the new `comments.controller.ts` docblock cites this very file). `docs/design/notifications.md:17` likewise says notifications are reported by the client "because comments live inside Yorkie CRDT documents", while the backend is now a second writer calling `NotificationService.createFromComment` directly. Both are contract descriptions left behind by the change; the docs-link lane only checks that backticked paths resolve, so nothing flags them.

samples.summary: The new server-side author-only edit/delete rule is not enforced on the editor's own CRDT path, which reaches the same threads
samples.evidence: `comments.controller.ts#assertCommentAuthor` introduces an author-only rule for edit/delete and states it "is made here rather than left to the UI". The other writer of the same data does not have it: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1313-1330`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:229,246` and `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:164,176` mutate `comments[threadId]` in the CRDT with no authorship check at all — the only gate is `CommentThreadCard.tsx` in the UI. Any workspace member with an editor session therefore still reaches the operation the new API check protects. Architecturally inherent to the CRDT (and acknowledged in the new docblock), so flagged rather than blocking, but the guard is one-sided.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `resolveDelete` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:78) gates only on truthiness of `root.tabs?.[tabId]`, and `applyDelete` (tab-ops.ts:102-106) then issues `delete root.tabs[tabId]` / `delete root.sheets[tabId]` inside `doc.update`. The DELETE handler (packages/backend/src/api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:161-193) feeds the raw URL param straight in, with only `assertSheetDocument` (workspace/doc-type) upstream — no key-membership filter. The same controller's duplicate handler at tabs.controller.ts:259 DOES use `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(root.tabs).includes(tabId)`, and the centralised helper at worksheet-lookup.util.ts:36-45 documents (lines 13-20) that a live Yorkie proxy answers `toJSON`/`toJS`/`toJSForTest`/`toString`/`getID` with truthy functions and that `in`/`Object.hasOwn` cannot substitute. The delete-on-absent-key failure mode is documented by this repo itself at comment-ops.ts:308-312 and modelled in comment-ops.spec.ts:154-162, so `DELETE .../tabs/toJSON` yields a 500 with an aborted CRDT transaction rather than a 404. `resolveRename` (tab-ops.ts:216, reached from tabs.controller.ts:131) carries the identical truthiness test. Greps found no tabId sanitiser anywhere in packages/backend/src and no other callers that pre-filter. This is a guard-with-a-bypass at sites outside the guard — in lane, and blocking at major.

finding.summary: New prototype-key tab guard is added only in the images controller; six sibling controllers reach the same `root.sheets?.[tabId]` write with the raw, URL-decoded tab id
finding.evidence:
The delta adds `assertPlainTabId` / `UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` to `worksheet-images.controller.ts` (worksheetOrThrow + getImages) with a docblock stating that `sheets['__proto__']` on a plain root answers `Object.prototype`, passes the truthy NotFound guard, and lets the write land on the prototype. Every other tab-scoped controller still has the unguarded copy of the same helper and the same write:
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-styles.controller.ts:54 (helper) → :94 `this.worksheetOrThrow(root, tabId).rangeStyles = rangeStyles;`
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49 → :106-110 `ws.charts = {}` inside `doc.update`
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:47 → :90 `ws.filter = filter` and :136 `ws.pivotTable = pivot`
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:57 (helper used by every PUT on column/row styles and sizes)
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-rules.controller.ts:59
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:158 / :193 (`root.sheets?.[tabId]` then `updateWorksheetCell`)
All six share the identical `@Controller('.../tabs/:tabId')` route prefix and identical auth guards, so the exact request the new images test refuses (`PUT .../tabs/%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F/charts`) still reaches these. `worksheet-structure.controller.ts:104-113` shows the safe pattern already in the repo (membership check against `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`). Fix belongs on the new code: hoist `assertPlainTabId` (or the key-membership check) into a shared helper — e.g. `sheet-document.util.ts` — and call it from every tab-scoped controller.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. There is no `assertPlainTabId`/`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` denylist anywhere in source (only in .agent-review JSON artifacts), and no per-controller unguarded tab helper. The tab guard is a single shared module, worksheet-lookup.util.ts:36-59, which does a key-membership test via `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)` (line 41) and 404s otherwise (line 57) — covering both the plain-root `__proto__` case and the Yorkie-proxy `toJSON`/`getID` case. All six controllers the finding names as bypassing import it and use it on exactly the write lines cited: worksheet-styles.controller.ts:17,79,120; worksheet-charts.controller.ts:12,88-91; worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:11,72,119; worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:16,118,161,204,247; worksheet-rules.controller.ts:21,83,126; cells.controller.ts:29,158,192,228. worksheet-images.controller.ts:19,63,95,97 uses the identical shared helper, so the claimed images-only asymmetry does not exist. A request to `PUT .../tabs/%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F/charts` therefore hits the same membership check and 404s. The only surviving raw `root.sheets?.[tabId]` accesses are comments.controller.ts:238 and :562/:567, and neither uses a URL-supplied tab id — :237 iterates `root.tabOrder` and :560 derives the id from `tabIdOfThread(doc.getRoot(), threadId)`; the URL-driven comment path uses `worksheetOrThrow` at :329/:333. The finding's own recommended fix (hoist into a shared util called from every tab-scoped controller) is already implemented.
